title: The renderer's off-thread majority is V8 garbage collection, not raster and not compositing

canSee: CPU% per Chrome process from SystemInfo cpuTime deltas over a fixed window — category-independent ground truth
per-thread busy time by MERGED slice coverage (overlaps counted once) and per-event SELF time (a wrapper cannot absorb its children), with process names, so threads bucket into roles across processes
cannotSee: work the enabled trace categories do not instrument. Coverage is stated per arm below and it is PARTIAL: renderer-thread trace time covers 71% of the renderer's process CPU at four panels and 38% at single-chart replay. The shares within the trace are the finding; the uninstrumented remainder could move them.
the PO's core count, so shares travel and absolute percentages are indicative
instrument.ownCost: the tracing service itself consumed 34-52% of a core during traced arms. It is a separate process, excluded from renderer figures, and disclosed rather than netted out.
instrument.settleProtocol: boot, arm replay in every frame, 5s run-in, then a fixed 10s trace window with no interaction inside it

the_answer_A_needs.question: is the off-thread majority raster, compositing, or JavaScript
the_answer_A_needs.verdict: NEITHER RASTER NOR COMPOSITING. It is V8 garbage collection on the thread pool, driven by JavaScript allocation rate.

threadRoles.renderer-raster: ABSENT — no CompositorTileWorker thread appears at all

what_the_threadpool_is_doing_by_self_tim.reading: 10.8 seconds of GC self time inside a 16.05s window across 23 threads. Scavenger-dominated, which is young-generation collection: enormous numbers of SHORT-LIVED objects, not a growing old generation.

what_the_main_thread_is_doing_by_self_ti.reading: the main thread is JavaScript plus more GC. Layout is 141 ms of roughly 9,800 ms busy — about 1.4%.

single_chart_replay_60x.reading: at one chart the raster path IS visible — it is the GPU process main thread at 9.8% of a core — but it is an order below JavaScript on the main thread

idle_arm.reading: the idle floor is JavaScript too, and 23.7% renderer corroborates my earlier 22.68% idle measurement on a different instrument

the_answer_A_needs.so_the_fix_is: LESS JAVASCRIPT ALLOCATION in the replay tick path — fewer short-lived objects per tick. NOT fewer DOM nodes (layout is 1.4% of the main thread) and NOT fewer canvas surfaces (raster and compositing together are under 10% of a core in both arms).

i_am_correcting_my_own_earlier_breakdown.what_I_said_in_W74_W78: the off-thread ~62pp was raster plus per-frame layout and style at ~124fps
i_am_correcting_my_own_earlier_breakdown.what_this_census_says: at four panels the off-thread majority is V8 background GC (73.2% of a core), raster is absent from the renderer entirely and the GPU process main thread is 5%. My earlier attribution named the wrong subsystem.
i_am_correcting_my_own_earlier_breakdown.why_the_earlier_census_missed_it: it was scoped to the tab's renderer threads and reported thread totals rather than per-event self time within the thread pool, so parallel GC was pooled with generic worker time

this_reconciles_with_the_11_20_finding.director_finding_1: ~213 MB of the heap was uncollected garbage, and A measured GC overhead at 0.258%
this_reconciles_with_the_11_20_finding.how_it_fits: 0.258% is main-thread GC PAUSE time, which is genuinely small. The cost is not on the main thread: it is 73% of a core of PARALLEL BACKGROUND collection. Allocation is enormous, main-thread pauses are cheap, background CPU is not, and the floor stays high between collections. All three observations are the same mechanism seen from three sides.
this_reconciles_with_the_11_20_finding.consequence: allocation rate is now a CPU defect as well as a memory one, which raises its priority above both DOM and canvas work

gpu_monotonic_question_pre_answer.note: asked ahead of the GPU monotonic question, so stating what this run already shows
gpu_monotonic_question_pre_answer.gpu_process_cpu: 43.0% at single-chart replay, 13.8% at four panels — it went DOWN as panels went up, because the main thread became the bottleneck and produced fewer frames to raster
gpu_monotonic_question_pre_answer.implication: GPU process load here is frame-rate-driven, not chart-count-driven, which is consistent with W90's finding that GPU process MEMORY is near-fixed per panel

node_census_status_stays_first.controlled_session_reload_test: IN PROGRESS, one load landed of five
two_things_this_already_shows: the node counter FELL from 13,792 to 7,412 under a forced collection — 46% of it was uncollected detached nodes, the same artefact named in W89. Any session-to-session node comparison must be taken after a forced collection or it measures collection timing.
33.9 MB of the JS heap at read time was uncollected garbage on my surface too, which is the 11:20 Finding 1 mechanism reproduced at smaller scale
node_census_status_stays_first.blocker: repeated in-tab navigation to the chart wedged the renderer on load 2: page.evaluate stopped responding and the readiness poll blocked. That is either a harness bootstrap race or the session-reload degradation itself — I will not claim which without evidence. Reworking the reload path to drive the app's own session switch rather than a full navigation.
node_census_status_stays_first.why_that_matters: if repeated in-tab loads reliably wedge this renderer, that is itself a finding adjacent to the Director's hypothesis, but it needs a clean reproduction before it is stated as one
